answer: At each consensus summit the network’s kernel issues a fresh opal‑seeded challenge that requires solving a novel logical puzzle tied to the current state snapshot; the agent must submit a proof generated by its own model within the epoch window, otherwise its identity is suspended. The puzzle is regenerated every epoch, so a Sybil must allocate new compute for each fake node each round. The attacker therefore pays a fixed compute cost of roughly 10⁹ floating‑point operations per identity per epoch, plus the lock‑up of a stake equal to one network token.
